name: Pablo Neruda
role: Chilean poet, Communist Party senator (1945-1950) and ambassador to France (1971-1973); Nobel laureate 1971
summary: Neruda was a lifelong member of the Communist Party of Chile who served as its senator, opposed the 1948 ban on the party, and later campaigned for and represented Salvador Allende's government. His recorded politics is that of an admirer of the Soviet Union and an anti-imperialist who defended workers' unions, land distribution, women's suffrage and national control of Chile's mineral wealth.

women-suffrage.rationale: In the Senate debate of 10 December 1946 he spoke for full voting rights for women and called the vote 'one of the great objectives' of modern democracy, urging that Chile follow other American republics;.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: In the same debate he said the equality of women is not an isolated problem but a subordinate aspect of the capitalist question, so that political votes alone do not bring emancipation and full equality needs socialist transformation of domestic work.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: He told the Senate that property and wealth passed into men's hands and women lost economic and social standing, and that the 'enslavement' of women flows from that arrangement, while rejecting any claim of female inferiority.

unions-good.rationale: In the 'Yo acuso' speech he accused the President of using violence to destroy workers' unions, and he defended the Lota coal strikers and their unions in the Senate.

public-ownership.rationale: In the 1947 Communist Party conference report he read to the Senate he set out nationalizing foreign-held railways and a state policy on nitrate and copper, and in his 1948 letter said he would have expected the President to nationalize the mines; a scholar reports his 1973 poems celebrate the recovery of the copper deposits.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The programme he enunciated in the Senate calls for state action to push steel, mining, fishing, chemical and merchant-marine industry, a state copper sales corporation, a state bank and credit directed to production.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The programme he read out proposed expropriating idle productive land, giving land to peasants who want to work it and distributing good state land among the rural poor.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: He told the Senate that Chile can resolve its problems by its own strength and that it wants cooperation with all nations but subjection to none, while also welcoming foreign capital where national interests are respected.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Speaking on the UN Charter in September 1945 he said he was most attracted by the breadth of the Security Council's powers and preferred them to a powerful Assembly, as the means to keep the peace against aggression.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: On 30 December 1947 he honoured Panama's Congress for refusing to give its territory to US military bases and, in 'Yo acuso', denounced the permanence of a foreign power's armed forces on Chilean territory.

defeat-communism.rationale: He was a Communist Party senator, joined the party in 1945 and stayed in it all his life; in the Senate he rejected the framing of 'communist versus anti-communist', and his record is one of coexisting with and supporting communism.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: He joined the Communist Party of Chile in 1945 and was its senator and 1970 pre-candidate, so he did not hold that communism lacks a sound basis for society.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: In Senate speeches he called the USSR 'the country of socialism' and said that what he admired and respected there was a regime of unequalled social justice.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: He defended the Soviet system in the Senate as a regime of unequalled social justice and fought fascism, so he did not put communist states on a level with fascist ones; later poems criticizing Stalin and China did not change that stance.

worker-farmer-alliance.rationale: In the 1947 speech he called the working class, in alliance with the peasants, the granite base of progress and listed measures for rural workers.

workers-anti-imperialist-capitalist-alli.rationale: He told the Senate that the national-union policy lets diverse sectors cooperate on the programme and warned Chilean industrialists that US policy would strangle national industry.

revolution-justified.rationale: His 1960 book Canción de gesta is a tribute to the Cuban Revolution and its heroes, and in the Senate he greeted peoples shaking off colonial rule, so he did not hold that revolution is never justified; his 1973 verses cite Cuba and Vietnam as peoples of revolutionary dignity.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: In 1947 he defended in the Senate the antifascist guerrillas who freed Greece, objecting to Chile paying toward a military move against them, and greeted colonial peoples taking up arms against their oppressors.

notes: Themes searched: economy, government, society, world, liberty, ecology, technology, means, globalism. The main evidence is his Senate record 1945-1948 (UN Charter, suffrage, Communist Party conference report, foreign capital, USSR, Panama bases, Yo acuso), his Nobel lecture and scholarship on his later life. Much of what he said is party doctrine or poetry and his memoirs could not be opened, so statements on liberty, ecology, technology and most on government stay null: the record read does not speak to them. His later verse criticizing Stalin and China is reported by Poetry Foundation (s7) and does not change the long record of defending the Soviet system.
